vocab-analogies.title: Analogies
vocab-analogies.html:
A : B :: C : ?  ·  + 10 relationships

An analogy asks you to find the same relationship in a second pair. Never look at the words alone. Name the relationship in one sentence, then test each option with it.

PAGE 1
Find the Relationship
Make a bridge sentence

Start here: The bridge sentence (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Say "A is to B as C is to D" and check the same rule holds.

1.1 The 10 common relationships

SYNONYMsame meaning happy : glad
ANTONYMopposite light : dark PART : WHOLE one part of the whole wheel : car WORKER : TOOL person and tool writer : pen WORKER : PRODUCT who makes what poet : poem ANIMAL : YOUNG ONE baby name cow : calf ANIMAL : HOME where it lives bee : hive
DEGREEweak to strong warm : hot CAUSE : EFFECT one causes the other fire : smoke
M E M O R Y H A C K | S A Y I T I N A S E N T E N C E

Make a sentence for the first pair, then reuse it. "A calf is the young one of a cow" → "A kitten is the young one of a cat."

PAGE 2
Tricks and Elimination
Test the options fast

2.1 Which option? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

The bridge sentence must work in both pairs word for word.

2.2 Rules that win marks

KEEP THE ORDERwhole : part stays whole : part car : wheel / house : door
SAME PART OF SPEECHnoun : noun, verb : verb run : walk needs shout : whisper
DEGREEweak → strong must match like : love / warm : hot TOOL : USE tool and its job knife : cut / pen : write SYMBOL : MEANING sign and idea dove : peace PLACE : PERSON work place court : judge / school : teacher STUDY : SUBJECT science and what it studies botany : plants
FEAR WORDSphobia : fear of claustrophobia : closed spaces
E X A M T R A P S W I T H

Order trap: if the first pair is part : whole, the second must also be part : whole.

Two close options: refine your bridge sentence ("a tool used to cut", not "related to") and re-test.

Not by topic: "doctor : hospital" is worker : workplace, not just "medical".

M E M O R Y H A C K | B R I D G E B O T H W A Y S

If your bridge sentence works for the first pair but only loosely for the option, reject it. Only an exact reuse wins.

PAGE 3

Traps, Practice and Recap

The mistakes examiners love, then test yourself

3.1 Solve step by step (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Name, test, mark.

3.2 Favourite exam traps
WRONG
RIGHT
WHYcalf : cow :: kitten : dog kitten : cat young one of wheel : car :: house : door door : house keep part : whole order hot : cold :: day : sun day : night antonym writer : pen :: painter : canvas painter : brush tool warm : hot :: cold : ice cold : freezing degree bee : hive :: bird : tree bird : nest home court : judge :: school : student school : teacher worker : workplace poet : poem :: writer : novel novelist : novel maker : product

3.3 Mixed practice: complete the analogy

1. Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ___

2. Fear : Courage :: Hate : ___

3. Page : Book :: Petal : ___

4. Knife : Cut :: Pen : ___

5. Puppy : Dog :: Cub : ___

6. Hot : Cold :: Rich : ___

7. Author : Book :: Sculptor : ___

8. Hand : Glove :: Foot : ___

9. Warm : Hot :: Cool : ___

10. Bee : Hive :: Lion : ___

Answers: 1 school, 2 love, 3 flower, 4 write, 5 lion, 6 poor, 7 statue, 8 shoe / sock, 9 cold, 10 den.

6 0 - S E C O N D R E C A P

Write a bridge sentence and reuse it.

Keep the order (part : whole stays part : whole).

Match the part of speech.

Degree pairs go weak → strong.

Exact fit only; reject loose options.

Common types: synonym, antonym, part-whole, worker-tool, young one, home.

vocab-antonyms.title: Antonyms
vocab-antonyms.html:
Opposites  ·  + prefixes & traps

An antonym is a word with the opposite meaning. CUET gives a word and four options. You pick the closest opposite in the context given.

PAGE 1
Opposite PatternsPrefixes, roots and shortcut pairs

Start here: Find the opposite (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Decide positive or negative first, then find the matching opposite.

1.1 Prefixes that flip meaning

UN- / IN- / IM-not unkind, incorrect, impossible
IL- / IR-before l and r illegal, irregular
DIS- / NON- / MAL-not, bad disagree, nonsense, malfunction
ANTI- / CONTRA-against antisocial, contradict
MIS-wrongly misunderstand
A- / DE-without, reverse amoral, deactivate

1.2 Must-know pairs

GENEROUS↔ stingy, miserly
BRAVE↔ cowardly, timid
ANCIENT↔ modern
ABUNDANT↔ scarce
OPTIMIST↔ pessimist
EXPAND↔ contract
VICTORY↔ defeat
ACCEPT↔ reject
M E M O R Y H A C K | P O S I T I V E ↔ N E G A T I V E

Mark the given word as + or −. The antonym will have the opposite sign and the same strength. benevolent (+) → malevolent (−).

PAGE 2
Tricks and TrapsContext, strength and look-alikes

2.1 Which option? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Eliminate synonyms and unrelated words first.

2.2 Rules that win marks

SAME PART OF SPEECHnoun ↔ noun success ↔ failure
STRENGTH MATTERSextreme ↔ extreme ecstatic ↔ miserable
CONTEXTmeaning can change by sentence fair (just) ↔ unjust, fair (pale) ↔ dark
WATCH NEAR-PAIRSsound-alikes confuse ascend ↔ descend
GRADABLEbig ↔ small, not tiny keep the same degree
ROOTSbene = good, mal = bad benefit ↔ harm
E X A M T R A P S W I T H

Synonym trap: one option is a synonym of the given word; never pick it.

Partial opposites: "rarely" is a weaker opposite of "often" than "never".

Look-alikes: stationary (still) and stationery (paper) are different words.

M E M O R Y H A C K | R O O T S H O R T C U T S

bene = good, mal = bad. pro = for, anti = against. ex = out, in = in. Know a root and you often know the opposite.

PAGE 3

Traps, Practice and Recap

The mistakes examiners love, then test yourself

3.1 Solve the antonym (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Positive or negative, then strength.

3.2 Favourite exam traps
WRONG
RIGHT
WHYgenerous ↔ kind generous ↔ stingy kind is a synonym brave ↔ bold brave ↔ cowardly bold is a synonym ancient ↔ old ancient ↔ modern old is a synonym abundant ↔ plenty abundant ↔ scarce plenty is a synonym expand ↔ stretch expand ↔ contract stretch is a synonym optimist ↔ hopeful optimist ↔ pessimist same meaning victory ↔ win victory ↔ defeat win is a synonym accept ↔ take accept ↔ reject take is a synonym

3.3 Mixed practice: choose the opposite

1. Generous: (kind / stingy / rich / noble)

2. Ancient: (modern / old / ruined / historic)

3. Abundant: (plenty / scarce / large / rich)

4. Optimist: (dreamer / pessimist / realist / fool)

5. Expand: (grow / contract / enlarge / extend)

6. Victory: (win / defeat / battle / glory)

7. Brave: (bold / timid / mighty / loud)

8. Accept: (take / reject / praise / allow)

9. Rapid: (swift / slow / quick / light)

10. Fertile: (rich / barren / green / soft)

Answers: 1 stingy, 2 modern, 3 scarce, 4 pessimist, 5 contract, 6 defeat, 7 timid, 8 reject, 9 slow, 10 barren.

6 0 - S E C O N D R E C A P

Mark the word + or −, find the opposite sign.

Eliminate synonyms (trap answers).

Match part of speech and strength.

Prefixes: un-, in-, im-, il-, ir-, dis-, non-.

Roots: bene = good, mal = bad.

Use context for words with two meanings.

vocab-synonyms.title: Synonyms
vocab-synonyms.html:
Same Meaning  ·  + context clues

A synonym is a word with the same or nearly the same meaning. CUET gives a word (often in a sentence) and asks for the closest meaning. Context decides, not the dictionary alone.

PAGE 1
Guess the Meaning
How to work out an unknown word

Start here: Guess the meaning from context (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Clue words, then roots, then tone.

1.1 Context clues

CONTRASTbut, however, although He was frugal, but his brother was lavish.
EXAMPLEsuch as, like, for example Rare animals, like the snow leopard.
RESTATEMENTthat is, or, in other words Candid, or frank.
CAUSE / EFFECTbecause, so Because he was ecstatic, he danced.
TONEpositive or negative sentence praise → positive synonym
ROOTSbreak the word into parts benevolent, malevolent
M E M O R Y H A C K | C L U E - W O R D H U N T

Look for but, like, such as, that is, because. They point straight to the meaning of the unknown word.

PAGE 2
High-Yield Word Groups
Words grouped by meaning

2.1 Which synonym? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Match the feeling and the strength of the word.

2.2 Word groups to remember

BIG / LARGEenormous, gigantic, colossal, huge colossal statue
SMALLtiny, minute, petite, miniature minute details
HAPPYcheerful, jovial, elated, content elated winner
SADgloomy, sorrowful, dejected, miserable dejected face
BRAVEcourageous, valiant, fearless, bold valiant soldier
CLEVERintelligent, shrewd, astute, sharp astute trader
ANGRYfurious, irate, enraged, livid irate customer
HARD / DIFFICULTarduous, tough, strenuous, laborious arduous climb
HONESTsincere, candid, frank, truthful candid opinion
E X A M T R A P S W I T H

One word, two meanings: fair = just OR pale; bear = tolerate OR animal. Use the sentence.

Opposite trap: an option may be an antonym; avoid it.

Strength: "furious" is stronger than "annoyed".

M E M O R Y H A C K | G R O U P B Y F E E L I N G

Learn words in families (angry: furious, irate, livid). One group gives you 4 to 5 synonyms at once.

PAGE 3

Traps, Practice and Recap

The mistakes examiners love, then test yourself

3.1 Choose the synonym (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Eliminate opposites, then choose the closest.

3.2 Favourite exam traps
WRONG
RIGHT
WHYfrugal = wasteful frugal = thrifty wasteful is the opposite candid = secretive candid = frank opposite arduous = easy arduous = difficult opposite elated = sad elated = joyful opposite colossal = tiny colossal = huge opposite valiant = timid valiant = brave opposite irate = calm irate = angry opposite vital = minor vital = essential opposite

3.3 Mixed practice: choose the closest synonym

1. Frugal: (wasteful / thrifty / rich / lazy)

2. Candid: (frank / secret / rude / shy)

3. Arduous: (easy / difficult / boring / long)

4. Elated: (joyful / angry / tired / lost)

5. Colossal: (tiny / huge / quiet / old)

6. Valiant: (timid / brave / weak / wise)

7. Irate: (calm / angry / happy / sleepy)

8. Vital: (minor / essential / hidden / odd)

9. Meagre: (scanty / plentiful / rich / bright)

10. Obsolete: (outdated / modern / useful / fresh)

Answers: 1 thrifty, 2 frank, 3 difficult, 4 joyful, 5 huge, 6 brave, 7 angry, 8 essential, 9 scanty, 10 outdated.

6 0 - S E C O N D R E C A P

Use context clues: but, like, such as, that is.

Break the word into root and prefix.

Match feeling (positive / negative) and strength.

Eliminate antonyms, which are trap answers.

Learn families: angry, brave, happy, clever.

Two meanings? Read the sentence.

vocab-idioms.title: Idioms
vocab-idioms.html:
Not Literal  ·  + 40 must-knows

An idiom is a fixed phrase whose meaning is not the sum of its words. "Kick the bucket" is not about a bucket. CUET asks you to choose the meaning of the idiom, so learn idioms in groups.

PAGE 1
Learn by Theme
Idioms grouped by idea

Start here: What does the idiom mean? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

If the literal meaning is silly, it is probably an idiom.

1.1 Idioms by theme

SUCCESSa feather in one's cap = an achievement hit the jackpot = win big
FAILUREbite the dust = fail or fall fall flat = fail completely
ANGERhit the roof = get very angry see red = lose temper
SECRETSspill the beans = reveal a secret let the cat out of the bag
HARD WORKburn the midnight oil = study late go the extra mile
TIME / LUCKonce in a blue moon = rarely a blessing in disguise

1.2 Idioms with animals and body parts

ANIMALSa wild goose chase = a useless search white elephant = costly useless thing
BODY PARTScost an arm and a leg = very expensive keep an eye on = watch
COLOURSgreen with envy = jealous in the red = in debt
M E M O R Y H A C K | P I C T U R E I T

Draw a silly picture of the literal words, then attach the real meaning. Let the cat out of the bag → a cat jumps out → a secret is out.

PAGE 2
Must-Know Idioms
High-yield list

2.1 Pick the meaning (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

The feeling of the sentence points to the idiom's meaning.

2.2 Idioms to memorise

A PIECE OF CAKEvery easy
BREAK THE ICEstart a conversation
CALL IT A DAYstop working
HIT THE NAIL ON THE HEADbe exactly right
IN HOT WATERin trouble
UNDER THE WEATHERslightly ill
BITE THE BULLETface a difficulty bravely
CRY OVER SPILT MILKregret what cannot be undone PULL SOMEONE'S LEG tease or joke
E X A M T R A P S W I T H

Literal trap: "raining cats and dogs" is heavy rain, not animals falling.

Similar-looking idioms: let the cat out of the bag (reveal secret) vs curiosity killed the cat (curiosity is risky).

Fixed form: do not change words; "break the ice" is not "break the snow".

M E M O R Y H A C K | S T O R Y G L U E

Make a mini story: "She was under the weather, so she called it a day, and the exam turned out a piece of cake." Three idioms, one story.

PAGE 3

Traps, Practice and Recap

The mistakes examiners love, then test yourself

3.1 Eliminate and choose (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Eliminate literal meanings first.

3.2 Favourite exam traps
WRONG
RIGHT
WHYa piece of cake = a dessert a piece of cake = very easy not literal break the ice = smash ice break the ice = start talking idiom in hot water = in a bath in hot water = in trouble idiom under the weather = outdoors under the weather = ill idiom hit the roof = climb up hit the roof = get very angry idiom spill the beans = waste food spill the beans = reveal a secret idiom cost an arm and a leg = injure cost an arm and a leg = very expensive idiom once in a blue moon = at night once in a blue moon = rarely idiom

3.3 Mixed practice: choose the meaning

1. A piece of cake: (a dessert / very easy / cheap / sweet)

2. To bite the bullet: (face pain bravely / shoot / eat quickly / cheat)

3. Under the weather: (outdoors / slightly ill / cold / happy)

4. To burn the midnight oil: (waste fuel / study late / cook / sleep late)

5. A white elephant: (rare animal / costly useless thing / big pet / lucky charm)

6. To hit the nail on the head: (be exactly right / hurt oneself / build / argue)

7. Once in a blue moon: (rarely / at night / daily / often)

8. To let the cat out of the bag: (reveal a secret / lose a pet / start a fight / run away)

9. A blessing in disguise: (hidden good fortune / a prayer / bad luck / a mask)

10. To cry over spilt milk: (regret the past / waste milk / be sad / cook)

Answers: 1 very easy, 2 face pain bravely, 3 slightly ill, 4 study late, 5 costly useless thing, 6 be exactly right, 7 rarely, 8 reveal a secret, 9 hidden good fortune, 10 regret the past.

6 0 - S E C O N D R E C A P

Literal meaning silly? It is an idiom.

Learn by theme: success, failure, anger, secrets, effort.

Fixed form: never change the words.

Match the mood of the sentence.

Eliminate the literal option.

Story glue: link three idioms in one story.

vocab-word-usage.title: Word Usage
vocab-word-usage.html:
Confused Words  ·  + 30 pairs

Word-usage questions test whether you can pick the right word for the sentence, especially look-alike and sound-alike words (affect / effect, principal / principle). Learn each pair by its one-line job.

PAGE 1
Confusing Pairs
Look-alike and sound-alike words

Start here: Which of the two? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Decide the part of speech first; it usually settles the pair.

1.1 Pairs with a one-line job

AFFECT / EFFECTaffect = verb (to influence), effect = noun (result) The rain affected the crop. The effect was bad.
ACCEPT / EXCEPTaccept = receive, except = but I accept the gift. Everyone except him came.
PRINCIPAL / PRINCIPLEprincipal = head, principle = rule The principal has high principles.
STATIONARY / STATIONERYstill / paper goods The car is stationary. Buy stationery.
LOOSE / LOSEnot tight / fail to keep loose shirt, lose a game
COMPLEMENT / COMPLIMENTcomplete / praise a complement of colours, a compliment

1.2 More pairs

ADVICE / ADVISEnoun / verb Take my advice. I advise you.
BREATH / BREATHEnoun / verb Take a breath. Breathe slowly. THEIR / THERE / THEY'RE owns / place / they are Their car is there. ITS / IT'S belongs to it / it is It's a dog; its tail wags.
THAN / THENcompare / time taller than; then he left
QUIET / QUITEsilent / very quiet room; quite good
M E M O R Y H A C K | A F O R A C T I O N , E F O R E N D

Affect = Action (verb). Effect = End result (noun). Smoking affects health; the effect is illness.

PAGE 2
Using Words Correctly
Test the word in context

2.1 Right word or wrong word? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Test the word by reading it into the sentence.

2.2 Rules that win marks

MAKE / DOmake = create, do = perform make a cake, do homework
SAY / TELLsay = words, tell = person say hello, tell me
RISE / RAISErise = go up, raise = lift something The sun rises. Raise your hand.
LAY / LIElay = put, lie = recline Lay the book. Lie down.
FEWER / LESScountable / uncountable fewer pens, less water
BESIDE / BESIDESnext to / in addition beside the door, besides Hindi
BORROW / LENDtake / give borrow a pen, lend a pen
HEAR / LISTENears / attention hear a noise, listen to music
SEE / LOOK / WATCHnotice / direct / follow watch a film
E X A M T R A P S W I T H

Part of speech: advise (verb) vs advice (noun).

Collocations: we make a mistake and do homework (not make homework).

Its / it's: apostrophe means "it is".

M E M O R Y H A C K | M A K E = C R E A T E

make something new (a cake, a plan, a mistake); do a task or a duty (homework, a favour, work).

PAGE 3

Traps, Practice and Recap

The mistakes examiners love, then test yourself

3.1 Fill the blank (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

The word before the blank tells the part of speech.

3.2 Favourite exam traps
WRONG
RIGHT
WHY
The rain effected the crop
The rain affected the cropverb = affect
I except your gift
I accept your giftaccept = receive
She gave me good advise
She gave me good advicenoun = advice
Its a lovely dayIt's a lovely day it is
He is taller then me
He is taller than mecomparison
The principle addressed us
The principal addressed ushead of school
This shirt is too lose
This shirt is too loosenot tight
She made her homework
She did her homeworkdo homework

3.3 Mixed practice: pick the correct word

1. The medicine had no (affect / effect).

2. I cannot (accept / except) this gift.

3. Take my (advice / advise).

4. The (principal / principle) is strict.

5. (Its / It's) a sunny day.

6. He is older (than / then) me.

7. My shoes are too (lose / loose).

8. The traffic was (stationary / stationery).

9. She is (quiet / quite) tall.

10. Everybody (accept / except) Ravi came.

Answers: 1 effect, 2 accept, 3 advice, 4 principal, 5 It's, 6 than, 7 loose, 8 stationary, 9 quite, 10 except.

6 0 - S E C O N D R E C A P

Affect = verb, effect = noun.

Accept = receive, except = but.

Advice = noun, advise = verb.

Principal = head, principle = rule.

It's = it is, its = of it.

Than = compare, then = time.

Make = create, do = perform.

vocab-spelling.title: Spelling
vocab-spelling.html:
Right Spelling  ·  + 30 tricky words

In a spelling question you choose the correct spelling or spot the wrongly spelt word. A few rules and a short list of commonly misspelt words earn nearly every mark.

PAGE 1
Spelling RulesPatterns for ie / ei, doubling and endings

Start here: i before e? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

I before E, except after C, or when sounded as "ay".

1.1 Rules at a glance

DOUBLINGone-syllable CVC words double the last letter run → running, sit → sitting
DROP THE Ebefore -ing make → making, write → writing
KEEP THE Ebefore -ment, -ful, -ly manage → management, hope → hopeful
Y TO Iconsonant + y happy → happiness, carry → carried
PLURALS-s, -es, -ies boxes, babies, heroes -FUL HAS ONE L not -full careful, useful, beautiful
M E M O R Y H A C K | I B E F O R E E

I before E, except after C. belief, achieve / receive, ceiling. And "ay" sound: weigh, neighbour.

PAGE 2
Commonly Misspelt Words
The high-yield list

2.1 Double letters or single? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

These three double-letter words are asked all the time.

2.2 30 words to memorise

A TO Caccommodate, achievement, address, beginning, business, calendar, committee, conscience, correspondence
D TO Mdefinitely, discipline, embarrass, environment, exaggerate, February, government, guarantee, immediately, maintenance
N TO Znecessary, occasion, occurrence, possession, privilege, receive, recommend, separate, successful, restaurant, unnecessary, until
E X A M T R A P S W I T H

Twin letters: accomodate → accommodate; occurence → occurrence.

Silent letters: goverment → government; Febuary → February.

Wrong vowels: seperate → separate.

M E M O R Y H A C K | S E P A R A T E H A S " A R A T "

separate: "there is a rat in sep-a-rate". And necessary: one Collar, two Socks (1 c, 2 s).

PAGE 3

Traps, Practice and Recap

The mistakes examiners love, then test yourself

3.1 Pick the right spelling (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Rule, list, then sound.

3.2 Favourite exam traps
WRONG
RIGHT
WHYaccomodate accommodate double c, double m occurence occurrence double c, double r recieve receive ei after c seperate separate a-r-a definately definitely finite goverment government govern + ment neccessary necessary one c, two s embarass embarrass double r, double s

3.3 Mixed practice: choose the correct spelling

1. (recieve / receive)

2. (seperate / separate)

3. (accommodate / accomodate)

4. (occurence / occurrence)

5. (definitely / definately)

6. (government / goverment)

7. (necessary / neccessary)

8. (embarrass / embarass)

9. (February / Febuary)

10. (beleive / believe)

Answers: 1 receive, 2 separate, 3 accommodate, 4 occurrence, 5 definitely, 6 government, 7 necessary, 8 embarrass, 9 February, 10 believe.

6 0 - S E C O N D R E C A P

I before E, except after C.

Double the last letter in short CVC words (running).

Drop e before -ing (making).

Y to i after a consonant (happiness).

-ful has one L.

Learn the 30: accommodate, occurrence, necessary, separate, government.

vocab-foreign-words.title: Foreign Words
vocab-foreign-words.html:
Latin / French  ·  + 30 phrases

English borrows words from Latin, French, German and Italian. CUET asks for the meaning of a foreign phrase or which phrase fits a sentence. Learn them by language and by use.

PAGE 1
Latin Phrases
The most-asked foreign phrases

Start here: Which language? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

The spelling often hints at the language.

1.1 Latin phrases you must know

BONA FIDEgenuine, in good faith a bona fide buyer
AD HOCfor this purpose only an ad hoc committee
PER SEby itself Money is not evil per se.
VICE VERSAthe other way round Ram likes Sita and vice versa.
STATUS QUOpresent state maintain the status quo
ET CETERAand so on pens, pencils, et cetera

1.2 More Latin

ALMA MATERone's old school / college
QUID PRO QUOa favour for a favour
AD INFINITUMwithout end
IN CAMERAin private
PERSONA NON GRATAan unwelcome person
CARPE DIEMseize the day
M E M O R Y H A C K | L A T I N = L E G A L & L O G I C A L

Latin phrases often come from law and logic: bona fide (good faith), ad hoc (for this), quid pro quo (this for that).

PAGE 2
French and Other Phrases
More words to recognise

2.1 Meaning by theme (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Group foreign words by theme to remember them.

2.2 French phrases

DEJA VUfeeling of having seen before
EN ROUTEon the way en route to Delhi
FAUX PASsocial blunder
RENDEZVOUSa meeting place
BON VOYAGEhave a good trip
CUL-DE-SACa dead-end street

2.3 German and Italian

ZEITGEISTspirit of the time (German)
KINDERGARTENchildren's garden (German)
A CAPPELLAsinging without instruments (Italian)
PRIMA DONNAa self-important person (Italian)
FIASCOtotal failure (Italian)
BAZAARa market (Persian)
E X A M T R A P S W I T H

Faux pas is a blunder, not a type of food.

Rendezvous is a meeting, not a rule.

Bona fide means genuine, not a legal trick: a bona fide buyer really intends to buy.

M E M O R Y H A C K | F A U X = F A L S E

faux pas = "false step" = a blunder. faux fur = fake fur. faux always means fake.

PAGE 3

Traps, Practice and Recap

The mistakes examiners love, then test yourself

3.1 Fit the phrase to the sentence (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Match the meaning to the sentence.

3.2 Favourite exam traps
WRONG
RIGHT
WHYbona fide = fake bona fide = genuine good faith ad hoc = forever ad hoc = for this purpose not lasting status quo = future status quo = present state as it is now faux pas = a dish faux pas = a blunder false step rendezvous = a fight rendezvous = a meeting
French meetingvice versa = in turn vice versa = the other way round reverse alma mater = old friend alma mater = old school nourishing mother en route = at home en route = on the way route

3.3 Mixed practice: choose the meaning

1. bona fide: (genuine / fake / old / late)

2. ad hoc: (permanent / for this purpose / free / large)

3. vice versa: (the other way round / in turn / next time / never)

4. status quo: (present state / future plan / past event / loss)

5. faux pas: (blunder / dish / dance / song)

6. deja vu: (a new idea / feeling of having seen before / a dream / a lie)

7. en route: (on the way / at home / in debt / at ease)

8. alma mater: (old school or college / foreign aunt / loud noise / soft toy)

9. rendezvous: (a meeting / a rule / a meal / a trade)

10. et cetera: (and so on / but not / at last / only)

Answers: 1 genuine, 2 for this purpose, 3 the other way round, 4 present state, 5 blunder, 6 feeling of having seen before, 7 on the way, 8 old school or college, 9 a meeting, 10 and so on.

6 0 - S E C O N D R E C A P

Latin: bona fide, ad hoc, per se, vice versa, status quo, alma mater, quid pro quo.

French: deja vu, en route, faux pas, rendezvous, bon voyage.

German / Italian: zeitgeist, kindergarten, a cappella, fiasco.

Faux = false.

Match the meaning to the sentence.

vocab-phrasal-verbs.title: Phrasal Verbs
vocab-phrasal-verbs.html:
Verb + Particle  ·  + 40 must-knows

A phrasal verb is a verb + a small word (up, down, off, out, in) that makes a new meaning. "Give up" does not mean "give". CUET asks you to pick the meaning or the correct particle.

PAGE 1
Verb + Particle
The verbs and particles CUET repeats

Start here: What does it mean? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

If the meaning is new, learn it as one unit.

1.1 High-yield phrasal verbs

GIVE UPstop trying Never give up.
LOOK AFTERtake care of look after the baby
LOOK FORsearch look for my keys
PUT OFFpostpone put off the meeting
CALL OFFcancel The match was called off.
CARRY ONcontinue carry on working
TURN DOWNrefuse turn down the offer
RUN OUT OFhave none left run out of sugar
GET OVERrecover from get over a cold

1.2 Particles and meanings

UPcompletion, increase eat up, speed up
OUTfinish, remove sort out, wipe out
OFFstart, leave, stop set off, take off, switch off
MEMORY HACK | VERB + PARTICLE = NEW WORD

Treat a phrasal verb as one new word. give up = quit. give in = surrender. give away = donate. The particle changes the whole meaning.

PAGE 2
Meaning and UseSame verb, different meaning

2.1 Which particle? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Particles carry meaning: up (finish), off (stop), out (discover).

2.2 Rules that win marks

LOOKlook after = care, look for = search, look into = investigate, look up to = respect
TAKEtake off = leave the ground, take after = resemble, take up = begin a hobby
PUTput off = postpone, put on = wear, put up with = tolerate
GETget along = be friendly, get over = recover, get away = escape
BREAKbreak down = stop working, break up = end, break out = start suddenly
RUNrun into = meet by chance, run out of = finish, run over = knock down
MAKEmake up = invent, make out = understand, make for = go towards
COMEcome across = find by chance, come up with = invent, come by = obtain
GOgo on = continue, go through = suffer, go off = explode
E X A M T R A P S W I T H

Look after (care) is not look for (search). Put off (postpone) is not put on (wear).

Separable: turn off the light = turn it off (never turn off it).

Put up with has three parts and cannot be split.

M E M O R Y H A C K | L O O K - A F T E R , L O O K - F O R

look AFTER a child (care, follow behind). look FOR a lost thing (search). look INTO a crime (investigate).

PAGE 3

Traps, Practice and Recap

The mistakes examiners love, then test yourself

3.1 Pick the phrasal verb (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Match the meaning to the phrasal verb.

3.2 Favourite exam traps
WRONG
RIGHT
WHY
She takes on her mother
She takes after her motherresemble
They put on the meeting
They put off the meetingpostpone I look my pen (search)
I look for my pensearch He looks the baby (care)
He looks after the babycare The car broke (stopped)
The car broke downstopped working

Turn it offpronoun in the middle

3.3 Mixed practice: choose the right phrasal verb

1. The match was (called off / called on) due to rain.

2. She (takes after / takes up) her mother.

3. Please (look after / look for) my cat.

4. He decided to (give up / give in) smoking.

5. We have (run out of / run into) sugar.

6. They had to (put off / put on) the meeting.

7. Can you (look for / look after) my keys?

8. I cannot (put up with / put out) this noise.

9. He (got over / got on) his illness quickly.

10. The car (broke down / broke up) on the highway.

Answers: 1 called off, 2 takes after, 3 look after, 4 give up, 5 run out of, 6 put off, 7 look for, 8 put up with, 9 got over, 10 broke down.

6 0 - S E C O N D R E C A P

Phrasal verb = verb + particle with a new meaning.

look after (care), look for (search), look into (investigate).

put off (postpone), put on (wear), put up with (tolerate).

call off = cancel, give up = quit.

Separable: turn it off.

vocab-rearranging.title: Rearranging the Parts
vocab-rearranging.html:
Jumbled Sentences  ·  + 5 clue types

In rearranging, a paragraph or sentence is broken into jumbled parts (P, Q, R, S). You put them in the right order. The trick is find the opening, then follow the linking clues.

PAGE 1
Find the Opening
Start with the right sentence

Start here: Which part starts? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

The opener is general and self-sufficient. A pronoun or linker cannot open.

1.1 Opening and ending clues

THE OPENERintroduces the person or topic fully Ravi is a student.
NOT AN OPENERstarts with he, she, it, this, these, however, but He studies hard.
THE CLOSERsummarises, concludes, uses so / thus So he passed.

1.2 Linking words that show order

ADDITIONalso, besides, moreover, in addition
CONTRASTbut, however, yet, on the other hand
RESULTso, therefore, thus, as a result
M E M O R Y H A C K | O P E N E R - P R O N O U N - L I N K E R

1. Find the opener (full noun, no pronoun). 2. Match each pronoun to its noun. 3. Follow the linkers. 4. Put the closer last.

PAGE 2
Follow the CluesPronouns, linkers and logic

2.1 Which clue to use? (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Pronoun, contrast and result clues fix the order.

2.2 Rules that win marks

NOUN BEFORE PRONOUNname first, then he / she Ravi came. He sat.
GENERAL BEFORE SPECIFICbroad idea, then detail Plants need water. Roots absorb it.
CAUSE BEFORE EFFECTreason first It rained. So we stayed.
TIME ORDERfirst, next, then, finally First ... Finally ...
QUESTION THEN ANSWERa question comes first Why do we sleep? To rest.
DEFINITE ARTICLEa first mention, the after A boy came. The boy sat.
E X A M T R A P S W I T H

Pronoun trap: a part beginning with "he" cannot be first.

Linker trap: "However" must follow an idea it contrasts.

Article trap: "A boy" first, "the boy" later.

M E M O R Y H A C K | A T H E N T H E

First mention takes a / an; the second mention takes the. A king ruled. The king was kind.

PAGE 3

Traps, Practice and Recap

The mistakes examiners love, then test yourself

3.1 Order the parts (follow the arrows)

decision flowchart

Opener, pronouns, linkers, closer.

3.2 Favourite exam traps
WRONG
RIGHT
WHYstarting with "He studied hard." start with a part that names the person pronoun cannot open starting with "However, ..." start with the idea first linker cannot open So he passed. in the middle So he passed. near the end result closes The boy ... then A boy A boy ... then The boy a then the It is a bird. before naming the bird name the bird first noun before pronoun effect before cause cause before effect logic order detail before general general before detail broad to narrow ending with "First,"
First comes earlytime word

3.3 Mixed practice: order the parts

1. P: He studied hard. Q: Ravi is a student. R: So he passed. S: He wanted to succeed. → order?

2. P: It rained. Q: We stayed home. R: So we watched TV. → order?

3. P: A boy came. Q: The boy sat. R: He smiled. → order?

4. P: However, he failed. Q: He worked hard. R: Ravi is a student. → order?

5. P: First, mix the flour. Q: Then add water. R: Finally, bake it. → order?

6. P: Water is vital. Q: It supports life. R: We must save it. → order?

7. P: She was ill. Q: So she rested. R: Meena is a girl. → order?

8. P: He won. Q: He trained daily. R: Arjun is an athlete. → order?

9. P: This helps health. Q: Exercise is good. R: Walk daily. → order?

10. P: Rahul missed the bus. Q: He reached late. R: Rahul left home late. → order?

Answers: 1 QSPR; 2 PQR; 3 PQR; 4 RQP; 5 PQR; 6 PQR; 7 RPQ; 8 RQP; 9 QPR; 10 RPQ.

6 0 - S E C O N D R E C A P

Opener: general, no pronoun, no linker.

Noun before pronoun.

General before specific.

Cause before effect; so / therefore come later.

A before the.

However follows the idea it opposes.
